newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Strong barriers loom on dollar's upside.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Strong barriers loom on dollar's upside.

text.p: With firm technical and psychological barriers looming for dollar/mark and dollar/yen, more consolidation could be in store for both rates in the short-term, chartists said on Wednesday.
They put firm resistance in dollar/mark at Tuesday's 34-month high of 1.7050 and said strong selling would probably surface to protect knockout options lurking just above that level.
Meanwhile, technicians said the market is fearful that the Bank of Japan could intervene to protect the yen above the 125 level. The dollar's recent peak against the yen was 124.82.
"I think we'll see more of the same," said Darren Spain, global foreign exchange analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston, referring to Wednesday's relatively narrow U.S. trading range.
The dollar traded between 123.75 and 124.48 yen in U.S. trade on Wednesday and edged higher from an early low of 1.6880 to poke briefly above 1.70 marks in the afternoon.
Thom Worden, a vice president in the global technical analysis group at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said he viewed the 1.70 dollar/mark level as a pivot point for the rate.

"My general feeling is that while we're below 1.70 we're still in a consolidation phase and we could see another test of (Wednesday's European) low of around 1.6810," he said. "If we get above 1.70 then you have to look for a push to new highs."
In the medium-term, or coming months, chartists said they were still targeting dollar/mark's February 1994 high of 1.7686.
